- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast growth to 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; force a 1–2 day lagged mean reversion to true price trend.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 units per day to account for event-induced volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to smooth out extremes; use sentiment-weighted moving average to preserve volatility structure.
